attacks.claim: In dark mode, `.day-card` keeps a hardcoded white background while its text uses `var(--text)`, which becomes near-white (#f2f2f7). Tile text, and the `.tile .meta` muted text, would be close to unreadable for the ~30% of users on dark OS mode. QA covered only light mode, so this is untested.
attacks.evidence: `.day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... }` with `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; --surface: #1c1c1e; ... } }`; QA: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"

attacks.claim: The 72px `position: fixed` action bar on mobile has no matching bottom padding or spacer on `.planner`/`body`. The last day (Sunday) and its tile Swap/overflow controls can sit under the bar and be unreachable or obscure keyboard focus (WCAG 2.4.11). Mobile is 68% of sessions, and the 360px width is not evidenced.
attacks.evidence: `.action-bar { position: fixed; ... height: 72px; ... }` and `.planner { max-width: 960px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 16px; ... }`; "Sunday is the last child of .planner"; ABSENT: bottom padding or spacer, and any 360px QA result

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" bulk-writes every planned recipe's ingredients into the user's list with no described confirmation, replace-vs-append behavior, de-duplication, or undo. Single adds get an Undo toast, but the bulk write, which changes more user data, does not. Repeated taps may duplicate items.
attacks.evidence: "'Generate shopping list' (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; "toast with 'Undo'" applies only to the single-recipe flow; ABSENT: confirmation, undo, or de-duplication for the bulk action

attacks.claim: The bulk add has no described timeout, retry, idempotency, or partial-failure handling. A mid-operation failure could leave a partial list with no stated recovery.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week); ABSENT: timeout, retry, idempotency, or partial-failure behavior

attacks.claim: The removal of the one-tap "+ List" button makes the most frequent planner action (~9.4/week per WAU, 64% on mobile) a multi-step path through a recipe page, Ingredients tab, and servings sheet. The stated decluttering goal conflicts with the usage data, and no per-recipe or per-day quick-add replaces it. The tradeoff is neither acknowledged nor measured.
attacks.evidence: "Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week ...)" vs. "The old tile-level '+ List' button is removed to declutter tiles." and "tap the tile → recipe page → 'Ingredients' tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → 'Add to list'"; ABSENT: per-recipe quick-add

attacks.claim: "Share plan" sends a user's weekly meal plan outside the account, but the artifact does not say what the link contains, whether it is public or unguessable, who can open it, or whether it expires or can be revoked. Shared plans can reveal household routines and dietary details.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Share plan</button>; ABSENT: share mechanism, visibility, access control, expiry, or revocation

attacks.claim: The release goes to 100% of web users in one step with no staged ramp or canary. The watch list names metrics but gives no baseline, threshold, alert, owner, or rollback trigger, so the flag-off rollback is not tied to any decision.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`"; "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate." (no thresholds or staged percentages)

attacks.claim: The rollback claim "same API, no data migration" is asserted without analysis of the data written by v7-only operations (drag-move between days, bulk generate, Share plan). Whether the old planner can read those writes is not shown, and the flag's per-user stickiness is unstated. With a 100% cutover, rollback is the main safety net, and it is untested.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"; "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it."; no rollback test cited

attacks.claim: Drag-and-drop moves between days have no described persistence, failure, or rollback behavior. A network error mid-move could leave client and server plans out of sync. QA reports drag as pass without covering failure cases.
attacks.evidence: "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it."; "Drag-and-drop between days ... VoiceOver: pass"

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" is a single action that adds every planned recipe at once, and the 100% simultaneous launch (Tue 10:00 PT) could create a load spike. The artifact gives no batching, rate-limit, or load-test evidence for the bulk endpoint, and no backend cost metric is watched.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with 'Generate shopping list' (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; ABSENT: load test, batching, or rate limit; "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: The new headline bottom-bar actions, "Generate shopping list" and "Share plan", have no QA evidence. The only shopping-list QA result covers the per-recipe path.
attacks.evidence: "Shopping list add via recipe page + undo: pass." is the only shopping-list item; no test is listed for "Generate shopping list" or "Share plan"

attacks.claim: The release bundles several independent behavior changes (action bar, drag-to-move, changed add-to-list flow, Share plan) behind one flag. These cannot be reverted individually, and the old planner's code path has no stated removal date.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`"; "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off"

attacks.claim: The Swap button has no accessible name identifying its recipe, and the toast with Undo is not described as a live region. Screen-reader users may not hear the add confirmation or the undo option.
attacks.evidence: "<button class=\"btn-ghost\">Swap</button>" (no aria-label); ABSENT: role="status" or aria-live on the toast

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" and "Share plan" are long labels in a 72px bar with a 48px primary button at 360px width, with no overflow or wrap rules. Truncation is plausible on the smallest supported screens.
attacks.evidence: `.action-bar { ... height: 72px; padding: 12px 16px; display: flex; gap: 12px; }`; no overflow or wrap rules; ABSENT: 360px QA
